title: Santa Monica Planning Commission Meeting January 21, 2025
description: Videos provided to you by the City of Santa Monica.
transcript_text: Mhm. >> What? Who's what? >> Jacob. >> This is Jacob. >> Yeah, I know. That's Jacob. >> I think we're going to we have quorum. >> Jacob is coming. >> Okay, uh I'd like to call the January 21st meeting of the Planning Commission to order. Um it is now uh 6:01 p.m. And um if we could all rise and um Commissioner Chaco, would you lead us in the Pledge of Allegiance? >> I pledge allegiance to the flag of the United States of America and to the republic for which it stands, one nation under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all. Okay, thank you very much. Um can we have a roll call, please? >> Yes. Uh Commissioner Fresco, absent. Commissioner Lambert. >> Here. >> Commissioner Landers. >> Here. >> Commissioner Reese. >> Present. >> Uh Commissioner Wasserman, absent at the moment. Uh Vice Chair Chaco. >> Present. >> Chair Hamilton. >> Here. >> Okay, thank you. Um we can now move on to agenda item four for the director's report. >> Yes, that'll be coming from me tonight. Uh Jing, uh sorry, our community development director will be out tonight. Uh so to kind of give a little overview of what is upcoming for the commission. Um on February 4th, uh we currently have no items, so we are anticipating canceling that meeting. Um on February 18th, there may be a airport conversion discussion that will be happening. Uh we're still trying to schedule that with the airport conversion team. Uh at the moment it'll be on the 18th, but we're also looking at March 4th. Uh that request came in only earlier this week, so we're kind of coordinating that effort. Um and then on March 4th, um we will be having hopefully the city manager uh coming to us this time. I know he tried um a handful of months ago, but unfortunately some scheduling conflicts kept him from joining us. Uh we will also be doing our uh annual legislative overview on what kind of all happened last year that is becoming effective this year. That will largely be a presentation on kind of future amendments. So we will not be voting on anything. It's more just letting you know what's coming your way. Um additionally, uh and I'll go in a little bit more detail regarding what happened at council on the 13th, uh but we'll also be having a study session of sorts uh regarding SB 1123. And I'll give you a little bit more information on that in a second. Um but also just going to reviewing our other boards and commissions that city planning oversees. Um for ARB, on December 15th, we had a pretty full agenda of four items. All were approved. Uh they consisted of an addition to an existing duplex, uh approval of a personal storage, which actually is a DRP that is before you tonight. Um there was also an eight-unit condo on 16th Street and an R1 modification at uh 2244 23rd Street. All approved. On January 12th, there was also another housing project at 2929 Pico for 59 units. That was also approved. And then looking into February, we have two additional housing projects. One on 26th Street, which is a 330-unit residential project. And another project, which is a single-unit dwelling and ADU. I know ARB doesn't typically review single-unit dwellings, but as this is in the uh potential historic South Beach District, all uh development goes before ARB, whether it's single-family or multi-family. So, that's why that one's a little bit unique. And typically, ARB does not review single-family homes. At the Landmarks Commission, uh the January meeting was canceled. So, the next one will be February 9th. Um largely, the discussion will be or the meeting will be around the discussion of the Mills Act program. Uh based on council's direction in October, um they asked us to bring back kind of a review of our program, what other jurisdictions are doing, um so they can have a discussion on future implementation. So, staff is is doing outreach now. They are going to the Conservancy tomorrow. Uh they will be going to Landmarks on the 9th on the 9th of February, ultimately to go to council on March to ask the question of what would they like us to continue to look into. Um but bringing back to City Council, so on January 13th, um, there were two item Well, there was two items regarding the cannabis equity program update. Um, that was largely based off a direction received from the state to realign our equity plan more closely to their requirements to ensure that if and when we wanted to pursue additional grant funding, whether the city or an applicant, we just aligned with the state. So, it was a very easy just kind of making sure we were compliant. Um, also we had a boards and commissions comprehensive review. Uh, largely there was no big changes to the boards and commissions that City Planning oversees. There was a discussion regarding the Landmarks Commission on to remove a, uh, residency requirement for five of the seven positions. Uh, during the study session, Council did not, uh, recommend did not pursue that recommendation. So, the residency requirement is still going to remain. Um, there was also the, uh, extension of the offsite affordable housing pilot program. So, if you might remember, uh, we allowed the pilot program to be, uh, projects up to a the first thousand units could apply. Uh, we got six projects in pretty quickly that capitalized on all those thousand units. And this was the discussion on if we wanted to continue that program, which Council, uh, voted to continue. Um, the last item, which is probably the most, uh, uh, of concern of people is we looked to, uh, repeal an existing emergency IZO and reaffirm a handful of Council's prior actions regarding some housing-related topics. Um, Council ultimately did vote to repeal the emergency IZO regarding SB 1123. That was the one that we, um, kind of started the process that we then came to you in November with. Um, but it was the IZO allowed for the addition of ADUs in these projects, and also gave you a handful of modified standards. So, that has been rescinded. No one took advantage of the emergency ICO while it was active, and it is no longer available for anyone to take advantage of, also. Um And then there was the handful of reaffirming votes. Uh three of them kind of regarding building and safety, the updating to the building code, aligning our high-rise definition to 75 ft with the state, and the uh continued adoption of our single stair ordinance. All were approved. Uh but the topic regarding around the resolution of intention about SB 9, 1123, and uh 684, our local implementation, uh Council uh ultimately did vote to continue the implementation process, but to align more specifically with state law, and to only uh review kind of trade-offs what uh additional standards might be needed in order to get an on-site affordable unit, or some type of affordable contribution, or what they kind of used as a family-sized unit. Um that is the topic that we will be bringing back to you on the 4th. It's a study session, but it's largely to help staff with the commission kind of hone in what are the parameters we should now go and look at. You know, they say family-sized unit, but but what is that? You know, what size is that? How many bedrooms is that? So, we can work with the commission to kind of hone in what we will then go and do feasibility analysis on, and then we will then ultimately bring that back for a true study session. But right now Council's direction was very broad, and so we kind of wanted to work with the commission to kind of hone in kind of where we should look. Um that is what happened at City Council. Um some of that might come in certain waves, you know, whether certain aspects of SB 9 come quicker versus 1123. We're still kind of gaming that out a little bit. Um and then lastly, just a update on what's going on in the city. I just wanted to make everyone aware that we have an interim city clerk, uh, Denise Anderson Warren, who was not the most recent city clerk, but the one before that, uh, will be serving as interim city clerk while we, uh, council >> process of managing ex parte contacts. Um, but, uh, and I'll I'll defer to Commissioner Wasserman to speak on this as well, but my proposal, and I would like to have them, uh, you know, for us to be able to ask staff to come back to us with language, is to add it to our rules of order that in these cases, when we start a hearing, when we come back from recess, and we're standing in the hallway talking with people, um, that the presiding officer at the time invites uh, voluntary disclosures related to interested parties. Um, that is a that would be a an obligation of the chair to to invite those disclosures. Choosing not to disclose would not jeopardize the proceeding in any way, um, and it would remain purely voluntary. Um, Jacob, do you want to Commissioner Wasserman? >> think that's right. I mean, I want to keep this I I do not want, when we do our next housing element, to have to disclose every single meeting I did, because every single person is an interested party in the housing [laughter] element. Um, but for the DA, for the pawn shop, I think that there is a clear interested party. Um, how you write that up maybe a challenge for you, or maybe you just leave it to Commissioner discretion, if it's voluntary anyway. Um, but yeah, I I do think the DA's felt weird, because we were there was clearly someone applying, we were meeting with them, and we did, I I think here, you asked us to, and we did, but we that wasn't in our rules of order. Um, so, I'd just like something to be in our rules of order about it. >> And I I will say that staff kind of understands the concern, and we can come back if we vote on this and it the motion passes, um, we can come back at the next meeting with some proposed language that we think would help address that issue. >> Do we have I just wonder if you have thoughts since we're presenting it for the first time? >> [sighs and gasps] >> Well, I you know, my thought I guess my thought generally is we already have volunteer voluntary disclosure requirements for everything that we do, um, whether it be a DA or otherwise. I think it really just comes down to us being uh forthright and transparent with any interests that we have in the particular matter and who we've already met with. Um, I think that's just the right thing to do. I I understand staff's concern about keeping it voluntary. Um, so to me it feels like more symbolism than substance, but I would support something that staff would put together to just help clear the air about what we should be otherwise doing no matter what. Is that right? Okay. Um >> I have a clarification. I presume that subject to however it's written, it would fall upon the chair to make a distinction between when there's a ex parte disclosure versus a voluntary disclosure depending on the circumstances where there may be an interested party. >> I I think that Well, so as as as a relatively new chair, I rely heavily on what the staff put gives to me. And I when there is a need and requirement for an ex parte disclosure, um, that's in the agenda and that's called upon. Um, when there is not, there's not. And so um, what what this motion would basically uh lead towards is uh before any discussion item, we would the chair would be prompted to voluntarily ask anyone if they need to make any ex any ex parte type >> No, they're not ex parte. We would not use the word ex parte in any >> Yeah. Then then some kind of disclosure whether we have met with or have personal interest in the matter before us. >> Yeah, and just to clarify, ex parte is sort of a term of art and it is required in quasi-judicial hearings. So, the chair's agenda will typically say this is a quasi-judicial hearing. These are the things that are required, legally required for those. Um, that would not be the case for the other amendments or discussions that you're talking about. So, those items would allow for the voluntary disclosures, which would be different than the ex partes. >> And and the personal interest piece is irrelevant to this. If we have personal interest, we have to recuse. That's that's a different story. But but but the the distinction is like I'm and I know the hour is late, but you know, when it's quasi-judicial, we cannot speak like we take a recess, we go to the bathroom, we cannot speak to anyone who is an applicant. It's literally illegal. Um, and if we do, we have to immediately report it so that the public is aware of what we discussed. In a context like we just experienced, right, where we wandered out on the break and there were the folks from the pawn shop who were like, "Hey, can we talk to you about this?" and we did it. I think that's I don't I don't have a problem with it, right? There's it wasn't illegal, but for the purpose of public process, I think at some level, the public has a right to know that we had some offline chats with people who had a direct interest in that text amendment. And we can make different choices about how much we disclose or what we disclose. And certainly, I can think of DAs where there are aspects of the work on the DA that I absolutely feel like I would need to disclose. And there are things that actually the public is best served when, you know, there are some informal conversations that don't get fully shared on the way. That's up to each commissioner to decide for themselves, but this would at least give the chair you'd have that line in your thing that says, "Hey, does anybody want to make some voluntary disclosures here?" That's it. >> Seems fair. >> Yeah. >> I think that Well, I mean it I I understand. Here's where where you're coming from, Commissioner Landers. I guess my concern is that we are going to be entering into a process that would be too bureaucratic. And um but I think before I you know, I'd like to see the staff recommendation about how we handle that without becoming without losing you know, without And it's late. I'm trying to >> I understand. >> without just losing the the the committee level conversations that we have. It's too bureaucratic, you know what I mean? >> Yeah. >> All right. >> Yeah. >> Totally. Um >> Ross wants to say something. >> a second, and then I'll do a vote. >> I'll I'll move that we um I'll move that we ask staff to draft um prospect proposed rules of order regarding regarding voluntary disclosures of inter- interested party contacts related to development agreements, general plan and zoning ordina- ord- ordinance amendments, and other legislative matters where um there may be a there may be specific interested parties as opposed to the public generally exception, which blessedly applies to the housing element. >> I'll second. >> Uh great. Uh Commissioner Landers? >> Yes. >> Commissioner Wasserman? >> Yes. >> Vice Chair Chaco? >> Yes. >> Chair Hamilton? >> Yes. >> That passes. >> Thank you. >> Item 14B. Uh Commissioner Land. >> I shared it. >> [laughter] >> You have it. >> Uh I item 14 C. >> Uh well, I also shared it. This is a a bit of a shot across the bow to mobility staff. Um they just reconstructed California and put back diagonal curb ramps. They're not legal. I hate going out into the street with a stroller. Um just when they come to us, I will have questions for them about that. >> I'll just if I can, I I was trying to save time, but on 14 B it's really that I understand that the conversations about 1123 and 9 and and and 684 are really all about missing middle housing and I just generally want to encourage us and the public to be looking around the country um at different ways that different states are approaching it and I shared it in particular because I thought there were some really cool-looking buildings um that were fully uh code compliant and development standard compliant in that context and um we ought to be trying to build those. That's all. Yeah. So, with that, may I move >> asking a question, I did look at what you you put out. >> And I my question would be were those two-story or three-story designs? >> Okay. >> They were two-story designs. >> Thank you. >> Um I will move that we adjourn with in memory of David Wasserman and Helen Wasserman and with sincere condolences to our colleague Jacob Wasserman. >> Second their loss. >> Thank you. His favorite Santa Monica establishment was Sidecar Doughnuts. Um did not ordinarily like doughnuts, but Sidecar did it for him, so we'll leave it there. >> Wonderful. All right, we are adjourned. Uh it is uh 11:12 p.m. >> We haven't had one of these in a minute. >> Mhm.
